question.problem:
Compute $P(X>6)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & x<1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6) & =P(6<X<\infty ) \\  & ={\int }_{6}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{6}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{6}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
